title: Brief to Live: a creator campaign day in under a minute
hook: A creator campaign day is four check-ins around the shoot.
caption:
A creator campaign day is four check-ins around the shoot.

Morning: the brief goes out with the must-haves at the top.

Midday: questions come back. If two creators ask the same thing, the brief has a hole, so the brief gets fixed and then the replies go out.

Afternoon: first cuts. Claim, product and ask get checked before the brand sees anything.

Evening: a follow-up by voice note, and every decision from the chat goes into one tracker.

The one to copy tomorrow is the midday rule. The same question twice is a note about your brief.

This is Brief to Live, a series on what happens between the brief and the ad going live.

script.setup: Idea: a brand or creative manager thinks a creator campaign is won on the shoot; the day is really run by four check-ins around it. On-screen title (first frame): 'A creator campaign day'. Expectation it sets: a quick look at what the day involves. The first line meets it; the video beats it with one rule the viewer can copy (the same question twice means fix the brief). Points are kept in the order of the day so the viewer can follow the clock; the strongest point sits second. Shot vertically on a phone with burned-in subtitles. Blur creator names, client names and chat contents.

script.notes: No numbers from the facts bank are used. Spoken at about 2.3 words a second for 45 seconds. Add a captions file for muted autoplay. Use the cover as the thumbnail.

notes:
CONFIRM WITH Shrutik: that the four check-ins (brief out in the morning, questions at midday, first cuts in the afternoon, follow-up and tracker in the evening) match how he runs a real campaign day, and that he can film it during a live campaign with creator and client details blurred. Nothing in the script describes a specific real day; he should adjust any step that is not true for him.
Reader: a brand or creative manager who has never seen the servicing side. Shape: a day in sequence with one rule to copy. Numbers used: none. Title changed from '60 seconds' to 'under a minute' because the script is 45 seconds.
